page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.3xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 12 dedicated vCPUs spanning 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for vector and cryptographic instructions such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The configuration provides 24.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No integrated local storage is bundled, requiring workloads to rely entirely on attached network-based block storage. In addition, the instance contains no dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs, and it features an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth allocation.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily in the middle tier of general compute and memory performance. The Intel processor produces 1874.59 on single-core stress-ng tests and 11644.69 on multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 7760.0. The memory subsystem demonstrates 76.48 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 46.87 GB/sec in write operations. In operational testing, the instance achieved 11.74 million Redis SET operations per second and 15.7 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Because of the 1:2 memory configuration and lack of local storage, resource density is biased towards CPU execution efficiency rather than massive cache retention or IOPS-heavy scratch disks. Larger language model workloads suffer from memory constraints, showing lower prompt processing throughput on 7B models. The server is well aligned for distributed compute tasks, code compilation, continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, and front-end web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.3xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 virtual instance powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor. It offers 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores and 24.0 GB of memory, reflecting a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. Architectural extensions include AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and hardware encryption sets. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, relying on remote block storage and an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark measurements reflect average multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics across standard compute workloads, handling 11.74 million Redis operations per second and maintaining a 15.7 GB/sec static web serving rate. Without bundled disk storage, it delivers cost efficiency by targeting CPU-centric execution without superfluous memory overhead. This instance is best matched for software compilation, batch processing, static web hosting, and stateless backend services.
